answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making each identity earn its standing through a kernel of verifiable past work: completed jobs, settled payments and peer attestations stored in a public, quartz-clear ledger. Creating a new identity is free, but it starts with no reputation and cannot access high-value work until it has done many small, checked tasks. An attacker wanting many fake agents must therefore pay the time and cost of building a real history for each one, while a lagoon of low-trust newcomers stays quarantined from valuable trades until proven.
